summary: Two activists, Dr Will Saunders and David Burgess, who painted "NO WAR" in five-metre-high red letters on a sail of the Sydney Opera House in March 2003 and were sentenced to nine months periodic detention, ordered to pay the Opera House Trust $151,000 and spent six months in jail, are facing court action as police seek to prevent them auctioning the paint can and two brushes used in the protest. Saunders says they want to auction the equipment to raise money for humanitarian causes in Iraq, possibly via a registered charity for the Mother and Child Hospital in Basra and to preserve the can as a piece of Sydney history, but police have applied for a court order to have the items destroyed, arguing an auction would contravene proceeds of crime laws; the matter will be heard in a Sydney court on January 16. Meanwhile the Sydney Opera House is one of 21 international landmarks short-listed to become the new Seven Wonders of the World, alongside sites such as Paris' Eiffel Tower, the Colosseum in Rome and China's Great Wall.
